entries.title: Library test: the Mudling (style key look)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ILLUSTRATION. Return exactly one image.

The attached picture is the style key. Paint one new picture in exactly its painting style: the same dense painted texture, fine brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm lamplight and crisp detail.

A MUDLING, a small friendly mud monster, knee high: a rounded lump of brown mud with a puddle base, two stubby mud arms, big round shiny eyes, a small open mouth, and a little green sprout with two leaves on top of its head. It stands on a plain flat magenta background, full body, facing the viewer, a curious friendly look. No other characters, no text.

entries.title: Library test: Mudling as a 2 x 2 grid, repainted over a soft underpainting
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ENEMY SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
The battle sheet of the enemy MUDLING (a regular enemy, level 1) for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: 4 poses of the same character in a single row. The game puts it in front of a painted background of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees, so its colors and handbrushed painted texture should feel at home there, painted in the same way as the area painting, but it must still stand out clearly against it.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. This is the painting style to match exactly: dense, jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light.
2. The AREA PAINTING of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees: the place Mudling lives and fights. Use it for the creature's world: its color palette, the color of its light and shadows, the dense handbrushed paint texture and the mood. Paint Mudling as a resident of this same picture, by the same hand: the warm key light stays at the upper left as described below, tinted by the area's light on its lit side, with the area's shadow colors in its shaded side, and its materials (moss, wood, brick, brass, glass, mud, cloth) painted brush stroke by brush stroke the way this painting paints them. Do not copy this painting's layout, buildings or props into the sheet.
3. A soft COLOR UNDERPAINTING of this whole sheet: the same 4 poses of Mudling, in the same order and in the same positions, blurred on purpose, like a painter's first block-in of color. It fixes each pose's shape, position, size, colors, face and expression, and nothing else. Paint the finished picture over it: repaint every pose in place, with the same layout, the same poses and the same character, and add the fine detail and brushwork the underpainting does not have, such as individual brush strokes, painted texture, highlights, crisp painterly edges and small painted details in the face and surfaces. The finished sheet is sharp, high resolution and richly detailed. Nothing from the underpainting is kept as it is: every edge, texture and highlight is freshly painted.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look handbrushed and painted by the same hand as the attached paintings: dense painted texture, visible brush strokes that follow the form, layered paint, fine detail, deep saturated colors, crisp painterly edges. Every surface of the creature (skin, fur, moss, wood, metal, cloth, glass) is painted with brush strokes, never airbrushed smooth, never glossy plastic, never a 3D render. The creature is painted into the same world as the area painting, by the same hand, so a viewer cannot tell the creature and the area were painted by different artists.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a creature, painted by hand with real brushes in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style, exactly like the illustrated school-yard painting of the style key and the area painting. Up close it looks like an oil or gouache painting on canvas: visible individual brush strokes that follow the shape of every form, layered paint, fine painted texture, small hand-made variations of color from one stroke to the next, and a faint canvas grain. Gently simplified shapes. Friendly-scary, funny and full of personality, never grim. This is a game for a family with a 6 and a 9 year old.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp, painterly edges with fine detail, formed where one brush stroke meets the next. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

THE CREATURE
MUDLING: a squat dome of wet brown mud with one green sprout on its crown, two small bright eyes, a tiny open mouth and stubby dripping mud arms. It is about 16 inches tall (1.3 feet), measured from its base or feet to the top of its highest point. For comparison, the smallest enemy in the game, the Mudling, is 16 inches tall.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A single image holding a grid of 4 equal square cells, 2 columns by 2 rows, each cell 512 x 512 pixels, so the full image is 1024 x 1024 pixels. The layout is exactly the layout of the underpainting. If your tool cannot make that exact size, keep the same 2 by 2 grid and make the image as large as it allows.
- Exactly 4 frames, one per cell, in reading order (left to right along the top row, then left to right along the bottom row), in the numbered order below.
- MUDLING FACES RIGHT in every frame (toward the right side of the image), as if facing the family on the right of a battle screen. Seen from the side or three quarters, slightly from above.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on the creature. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on its edges. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.
- Same scale in every cell, exactly the scale and position of the figures in the underpainting, which already fills each cell as much as its widest pose allows. In every cell the feet or base rest on the same horizontal line as in the underpainting, with a small soft contact shadow directly under it. Nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.
- Draw ONLY MUDLING. No effects, motion lines, sparkles, other characters, props that are not part of it, text or word balloons.
- The same colors, details and level of painted detail in every frame.

THE 4 FRAMES
1. STANCE: battle stance, idle and ready, weight settled.
2. FLINCH: startled by a hit, recoiling a little, eyes shut or squinting.
3. ATTACK A: the wind-up for its signature attack, Mud Pie.
4. ATTACK B: the attack landing.

Family friendly for ages 6 and up. Keep the flinch frame comic, never grim.

NEVER substitute. Do not add extra frames, merge two frames or repeat a pose. If anything is unclear, draw MUDLING in the pose described, facing right, with the shape and colors of the likeness in attachment 3.

entries.title: Grace walk TEST: one 3 x 3 sheet, built like Tom's walk sheet (11-04)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE CHARACTER WALK SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

ATTACH: the hero pose picture of Grace (the reference).

WHAT THIS IS
Walking frames for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game. The character is Grace, a bright, bossy nine-year-old niece. The attached hero pose is the reference for Grace. Draw her EXACTLY like the reference in every frame: same face, hair, clothes, colors, proportions, art style, level of detail. Keep the face as faithful to the reference as it is in the hero pose, in every frame, including from the side and from behind where hair and ears show.

GRACE'S LOOK (same as the reference)
Long straight honey-brown hair with golden highlights, falling past her shoulders. Warm brown eyes, a big happy smile, small teal stud earrings. Oversized lavender crew-neck sweatshirt with long sleeves (plain on the back), baggy heather-gray sweatpants, pink and silver glitter sneakers with white soles. A small gold soup dumpling squishy studded with diamonds hangs from a short chain at her left hip. Hands empty.

ART STYLE
- A richly detailed hand-painted digital illustration of a real child, exactly like the attached picture, shown full body. Smooth blended brushwork, glossy highlights on skin and hair, finely painted hair strands. Clothing and fabric are drawn in fine detail.
- Caricature proportions: a big head, a slim body, small hands and small feet, large expressive eyes and a warm, slightly exaggerated expression. The head is exactly the size it is in the reference. The face keeps a clear likeness of the reference.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow on the skin, a gentle rim light, saturated jewel-toned colors.
- Crisp clean silhouettes. No thick or black outlines.
- Painted, realistic. NOT pixel art, NOT 16-bit. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette, no flat cartoon shading, no anime style.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A grid of 3 columns by 3 rows of equal square cells, 256 x 256 pixels each, so the full image is 768 x 768. If your tool offers a different size, keep exactly 3 columns and 3 rows of equal square cells.
- Exactly 9 frames, one per cell, filled left to right, top to bottom, in the numbered order below.
- Camera: a character turnaround at about chest height, full body, straight on for the front and back rows and a true side profile for the third row. No top-down angle.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere in the character. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on the character's edges, hair strands or flyaway hairs. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.

Create the actual environment painting for Area 01, The Square, from The Adventures of Tom, a family role-playing game. Generate the image now. Do not make a plan, presentation, diagram, infographic, example sheet, or project update.

One standalone, edge-to-edge, full-frame environmental painting. No border, title, labels, captions, grid, pins, UI, inset views, or white page. Landscape canvas, 1920 x 1664 pixels (15:13). If your tool cannot produce that exact size, use the closest landscape aspect at the highest resolution.

STYLE AND CAMERA
A richly detailed, polished hand-painted digital illustration of a small town square, like premium mobile game environment art. Smooth blended brushwork, glossy highlights on roof tiles, lanterns and water, saturated jewel-toned colors, crisp clean silhouettes, fine detail on every surface. Fixed elevated three-quarter camera looking down into the scene at about 35 degrees, showing building fronts, roofs and walkable paving together. Same camera across the whole uninterrupted scene. No photorealism, no plastic 3D look, no top-down floor plan, no visible pixels, no thick black outlines.

SETTING
A friendly small Long Island town square on a clear warm afternoon. Golden sunlight from the upper left, long soft shadows falling to the lower right, faint lilac light in the shade. Honey-cream cobblestone paving, mature leafy trees, low wooden fences, flower barrels and planters. Small-town coziness, not a palace or a city.

THIS IS A WALKABLE GAME MAP: NAVIGATION COMES FIRST
A character must be able to walk from any exit to every door and all the way around every building. No building, fence, tree or prop may wall off a route.
- Every building is FREESTANDING and NARROW, about one sixth of the image width. No two buildings touch. Between every pair of neighbouring buildings there is a wide cobblestone alley, at least half a building wide, open from the front of the buildings to the back.
- North row: the alley between buildings 1 and 2 is the stone stairway lane that climbs to the TOP edge exit. The alleys between 2 and 3 and between 3 and 4 lead to a narrow cobbled garden path that runs BEHIND the whole north row, so you can circle every north building.
- South row: three wide alleys run straight DOWN from the plaza, between buildings 5 and 6, between 6 and 7, and between 7 and 8, to a cobbled lane that runs along the fronts of the south row. The alley between 6 and 7 is the widest and continues straight down to the BOTTOM edge exit.
- The broad plaza lane runs to the RIGHT edge exit. There is also open paving between building 8 and the right edge, linking the plaza to the lower lane.
- Benches, barrels, lamps, trees and the taxi sit beside the paths, never in them. No exit on the left edge.

ARCHITECTURE: EXACTLY EIGHT DISTINCT, STRONGLY THEMED BUILDINGS
Every building must be unmistakably its shop even with no sign: the theme is built into its shape, roofline, windows, trim and materials, not just props by the door. No two buildings share a silhouette. No generic cottages.
Four buildings along the NORTH side, left to right, doors facing the plaza below them:
1. Crumb Bakery (terracotta and golden crust-brown roof, honey walls): a plump rounded roof like a loaf of bread, a big brick bread-oven chimney puffing warm steam, a round oven-door window, iced-cake trim along the cornice, a striped awning over a window of bread and pastries, bread racks and flour sacks outside.
2. Hush Library (dusty lavender roof, cream stone): a tall quiet building whose front is shaped like a row of giant book spines in leather colors, page-edged cream trim under the eaves, a carved stone owl on the roof peak, tall arched windows full of shelves, a small reading bench under a window.
3. Sprout House (green roof, sage walls): a building half swallowed by plants, living grass and flowers growing on the roof, a glass greenhouse dome, vines and trellis over the walls, seedling trays, watering cans and a wheelbarrow of soil by the door.
4. Penny's Pockets (coral-red roof, butter walls): an adventurer's outfitter and snack shop, backpacks, satchels, lanterns, rope and walking sticks hanging on the outside wall, a scalloped awning shaped like rows of pockets, a deep bay window of snack crates and candy jars, copper penny studs on the door, a pot of marigolds.
Four buildings along the SOUTH side, left to right, doors facing the lower lane in front of them:
5. Snail Mail (slate-blue roof, parchment walls): a post office with a curled snail-shell spiral built into its front, a round spiral window, a short spiral turret with a metal snail weathervane, rows of brass letter slots, parcels and mail sacks by the door, a red mailbox and a blue drop box.

7. Moon Club (silver dome, night-blue walls): a faded, once-glamorous 1930s observatory lounge, a small silver observatory dome on the roof with a telescope poking out, walls painted with tiny gold stars, gold art-deco trim, a round porthole window, , a brass globe and a telescope outside.
8. Long Island Taxi Co. (yellow-ochre roof, ivory walls): a little dispatch garage, a black-and-yellow checkered band around the walls, a door for customers to enter, a clock over the window, a tire stack at the side.
No ninth building, no clock tower, hall, gazebo or mansion. there must be a clear path between Kettle Cottage and the Moon Club leading to the fountain.

Each building has one sign, a unique object designed in that building's own theme, shape and materials, never a plain plaque, with lettering designed to match. ALL CAPITALS, two lines unless noted, spelled exactly as written, letter by letter, large and easy to read. Signs never cover a door, awning or lamp.
1. CRUMB / BAKERY: a hanging carved wooden loaf of bread, letters piped in cream icing.
2. HUSH / LIBRARY: a gilded open-book plaque, letters engraved in gold.
3. SPROUT / HOUSE: a leaf-shaped wooden board wrapped in vines, letters painted fresh green.
4. PENNY'S / POCKETS: a huge round copper penny hanging from an iron bracket, letters stamped into the coin.
5. SNAIL / MAIL: an envelope-shaped board with a red wax seal, letters in navy postal capitals.
6. KETTLE / COTTAGE: a hanging teapot-shaped painted sign, letters in rose and cream.

PLAZA
A wide paved plaza between the two rows. A LARGE round stone fountain, about one fifth of the image width, with a lower basin, a tiered spout and flowers around it, sits just left of the center with open paving all around it. Two wooden benches with flower barrels, one left and one right of the fountain. Iron street lamps along the plaza. Dense summer trees and wooden fences around the outer edges, leaving the three exits open.

STRICT EXCLUSIONS

A whole game map seen from high up, like a drone shot of the entire hollow, with a wide margin of forest on every side. Do not zoom in on a corner. Do not crop any landmark at an edge.

A grown-up person on a path is about one fifteenth of the picture height.
The stone path is about two people wide.
The exit board is about one seventh of the picture width.
The muddy clearing is wide and open, about one third of the picture width.
The pond fills the upper right and top center, about four tenths of the picture width.

SETTING
A soggy, slightly spooky but friendly woodland hollow at the edge of a small Long Island town, on a warm afternoon. Soft even daylight through the leafy canopy, with gentle shadows falling straight down under the trees. A big murky green pond with lily pads and cattails, mossy logs, old stumps, mud puddles, ferns, mushrooms and mossy boulders. Cozy and mischievous, never scary.

LAYOUT (this is a walkable game map)

ENTRANCE: a stone path with worn steps enters from the BOTTOM edge, a little left of center, between two low wooden fence sections about one person tall.
The stone path climbs straight up into a WIDE OPEN MUDDY CLEARING in the middle of the picture.
From the clearing, a branch runs LEFT to a soggy bench nook on the left side, and another branch runs RIGHT to Boppy’s fishing spot on the pond shore.
THE POND: no path goes into the water. Its lower and left shores are walkable mud.
The left, top and right edges are a solid wall of dense forest: thick trees, boulders, brambles and undergrowth, with no break, no opening and no path reaching any edge except the bottom.
Logs, stumps, rocks, ferns and cattails sit beside the paths, never across them.

LANDMARKS AND PROPS

Soggy bench nook (left side): an old wooden bench sinking a little into the mud, puddles around its feet, moss on the slats.
Boppy’s fishing spot (right side, pond shore): a small weathered wooden bench with a thermos, a metal bucket and a fishing rod leaning on it, facing the water.
Around the pond: lily pads, cattails, a half-sunken mossy log, ripples, a few water lilies.
Mossy boulders, old stumps, clumps of mushrooms, ferns, wildflowers.

THE EXIT BOARD (the only sign in the image)
One exit board, hung high between two tall stout wooden posts on either side of the stone path, like a gate header. Board center about four fifths of the way down the picture, about 340 x 108 px at full size, with a thin carved wooden frame. Face deep forest green (about 
#2F4A35) with a thin gold inner line. Lettering cream-gold (about 
#F2E6B8) with a thin dark green outline, hand-painted signwriter capitals, bold and slightly rounded. Two centered lines, ALL CAPITALS, same letter height, spelled exactly letter by letter:
THE SQUARE / SHOPS
Nothing else on the board: no arrows, numbers, icons or flourishes. The stone path and steps stay open and clear under the board, continuing to the bottom edge.

LAYERING
Mud, grass and stone path continue unbroken under and behind every tree, post, bench and boulder. Every tall object has a clear visible base with ground showing behind it. Crisp clean silhouettes on tree canopies, the board and posts. Nothing floats.

COLORS
Soft golden light 
#FFE1A0, warm brown mud and trail 
#A47B52, mossy green 
#608775, murky pond green 
#4E7A5E, light green grass 
#B4C395, warm shadows 
#716351. Clear darker contact shadow under trees and props.

STRICT EXCLUSIONS
No people, animals, monsters, frogs or fish. No chests, items, keys, coins, switches or collectibles. No words, numbers or logos other than the exit board. No buildings, bridges, boats, gates or locks. No light beams, sun shafts or glowing gaps anywhere. No grid, colored tiles, diamonds, numbered markers, map or diagram look. No title card, frame, contact sheet or palette chart.

Deliver the single environment painting itself. Do not replace the painting with a description of it.

Two things to check on the result: the top-left corner should be solid forest, and the bottom stone path should be the only opening. If either fails, send me the image and I’ll look at what the generator did before changing anything else.

- Hand-painted storybook style grown up into rich painted detail: dense jewel-toned painted texture, visible brush texture, soft edges, believable warm light, the look of a lovingly painted adventure game location. NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art.
- A TOUCH MUTED. This is a backdrop, and game characters will stand in front of it, so they must pop. Lower the saturation about 20% from what you would normally paint. Compress the contrast: the darkest darks no darker than about 15% brightness, the lightest lights no brighter than about 92%. No pure white, no pure black, no neon, no small bright accents.
- Detail is richest in the upper band and gets quieter toward the floor. Soft light, no hard cast shadows.

CAMERA (the most important rule)
- One fixed camera, facing the back wall straight on, a little above floor level and looking slightly down (about 30 degrees), the way a classic role-playing game battle screen looks. PARALLEL projection: every vertical edge perfectly vertical, every horizontal edge perfectly horizontal, NO vanishing point, no wide-angle, fisheye or tilt-shift, no rotation, no diagonal composition.
- The back wall and scenery face the camera flat. No side walls angling in.
- The horizon, where the floor meets the wall or scenery, is ONE perfectly straight horizontal line at y = 590 (55% down from the top), the same height across the whole width.

GROUND RULES (so characters standing on it look planted, not floating)
1. Everything below y 590 is open, flat, walkable floor, from the left edge to the right edge and down to the bottom edge. One continuous surface with nothing standing on it.
2. The floor is MATTE. No mirror, gloss, wet look, reflections, window or light streaks, spotlight pools or glow circles. Light never pools on it.
3. Floor brightness is mid-value (about 40 to 65%), the same from left to right, and changes by no more than about 10% from the horizon to the bottom edge. No vignette, no dark corners, no darkening toward the edges.
4. Floor texture is low contrast (grain, planks or tiles differ by no more than about 8% in brightness) and evenly scaled everywhere. Any seam lines run perfectly horizontal and vertical, evenly spaced, never converging. No diagonal or radial patterns, no inlay shapes, no rug or carpet edges, no borders, stripes, arrows or floor markings.
5. Below y 590 there are NO props of any kind: no rails, tracks, pipes, cables, steps, curbs, drains, puddles, plants, rocks, leaves, furniture, railings or debris.
6. Nothing painted on the floor may look like a character, a character's shadow, a footprint or a spot to stand. Only a very soft, thin darkening where the floor meets the wall is allowed.
7. No foreground framing: no railing, tree trunk, furniture, plant, curtain or architecture may cross y 590 or touch the bottom edge. Framing elements at the far left or far right are allowed only above y 560 and within 220 px of that edge.

KEEP CALM BEHIND THE CHARACTERS (so they stand out)
- Two broad bands, x 150 to 1050 and x 1340 to 1780, between y 330 and y 590, are where character bodies will stand in front of the scenery. Keep the scenery there mid-tone and low contrast: no pure white or near-black shapes, no bright or saturated spots, no strong light source (lamp, window, sun, fire), no busy patterns, no faces, no text.
- Put the brightest lights and the richest detail above y 330, and keep the main landmark near the horizontal center of the picture.
- The top strip (y 0 to 100) and the top-right corner (x 1500 to 1920, y 0 to 190) stay quiet: low detail, no landmarks, no bright spots, no text. Game buttons and banners are drawn there.

DO NOT ADD
No people, characters, creatures, animals or silhouettes. No text or letters except where this prompt asks for specific words, and then spell them exactly. No logos, UI, menus, frames or watermarks. No foreground objects. Nothing below y 590 except the floor.

OUTPUT: one image, 1920 x 1080 px, PNG.

Do not paint a full panorama: the town is a thin band and the rest of the picture is plain sky.

THE SKY: everything above the band is ONE smooth empty midday gradient, soft blue at the top easing to pale warm cream just above the trees, with nothing in it: no clouds, no sun, no birds, no haze bank, no second horizon, no distant hills.

STYLE
Hand-painted storybook style grown up into rich painted detail: dense jewel-toned painted texture, fine brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm golden light from the upper left, soft warm rim light, no thick outlines. NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art. No people, no text, no letters, no signs, no logo, no watermark, no border.

entries.title: Library test: Pond Grump as a 2 x 2 grid, matte and handbrushed finish copied from an approved picture
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ENEMY SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
The battle sheet of the enemy POND GRUMP (a regular enemy, level 1) for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: 4 poses of the same character in a single row. The game puts it in front of a painted background of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees, so its colors and handbrushed painted texture should feel at home there, painted in the same way as the area painting, but it must still stand out clearly against it.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. This is the painting style to match exactly: dense, jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light.
2. The AREA PAINTING of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees: the place Pond Grump lives and fights. Use it for the creature's world: its color palette, the color of its light and shadows, the dense handbrushed paint texture and the mood. Paint Pond Grump as a resident of this same picture, by the same hand: the warm key light stays at the upper left as described below, tinted by the area's light on its lit side, with the area's shadow colors in its shaded side, and its materials (moss, wood, brick, brass, glass, mud, cloth) painted brush stroke by brush stroke the way this painting paints them. Do not copy this painting's layout, buildings or props into the sheet.
3. A soft COLOR UNDERPAINTING of this whole sheet: the same 4 poses of Pond Grump, in the same order and in the same positions, blurred on purpose, like a painter's first block-in of color. It fixes each pose's shape, position, size, colors, face and expression, and nothing else. Paint the finished picture over it: repaint every pose in place, with the same layout, the same poses and the same character, and add the fine detail and brushwork the underpainting does not have, such as individual brush strokes, painted texture, highlights, crisp painterly edges and small painted details in the face and surfaces. The finished sheet is sharp, high resolution and richly detailed. Nothing from the underpainting is kept as it is: every edge, texture and highlight is freshly painted.
4. A FINISHED picture of a different creature, painted in exactly the surface finish wanted for this sheet: matte, with visible brush strokes, ridges of paint, layered color and a canvas grain. Use it ONLY for how the paint looks (the matte finish, the brushwork, the sharpness of the edges). Do not copy its creature, pose or layout: the creature, poses and layout come only from attachment 3.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look handbrushed and painted by the same hand as the attached paintings: dense painted texture, visible brush strokes that follow the form, layered paint, fine detail, deep saturated colors, crisp painterly edges. Every surface of the creature (skin, fur, moss, wood, metal, cloth, glass) is painted with brush strokes, never airbrushed smooth, never glossy plastic, never a 3D render. The creature is painted into the same world as the area painting, by the same hand, so a viewer cannot tell the creature and the area were painted by different artists.

SURFACE AND BRUSHWORK (the most important instruction)
Every surface is matte, like dry oil paint or gouache on canvas. Light is shown by broad, soft highlights built from visible brush strokes with dry-brush texture along their edges. Brush strokes are clearly visible everywhere and vary in size: broad strokes for the large forms, short flicks for texture, thick ridges of paint on the lit side of every form. Color is built in layers, so warm and cool tones show through each other. Edges are painted crisp with a small brush. A fine canvas weave grain lies over the whole picture. NOT glossy, NOT wet-looking, NOT plastic, NOT airbrushed, NOT a 3D render.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a creature, painted by hand with real brushes in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style, exactly like the illustrated school-yard painting of the style key and the area painting. Up close it looks like an oil or gouache painting on canvas: visible individual brush strokes that follow the shape of every form, layered paint, fine painted texture, small hand-made variations of color from one stroke to the next, and a faint canvas grain. Gently simplified shapes. Friendly-scary, funny and full of personality, never grim. This is a game for a family with a 6 and a 9 year old.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp, painterly edges with fine detail, formed where one brush stroke meets the next. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

THE CREATURE
POND GRUMP: a fat round-shouldered mossy olive-green toad lump with a pale sagging belly, pondweed hanging like wet hair and a permanent scowl. It is about 24 inches tall (2 feet), measured from its base or feet to the top of its highest point. For comparison, the smallest enemy in the game, the Mudling, is 16 inches tall.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A single image holding a grid of 4 equal square cells, 2 columns by 2 rows, each cell 512 x 512 pixels, so the full image is 1024 x 1024 pixels. The layout is exactly the layout of the underpainting. If your tool cannot make that exact size, keep the same 2 by 2 grid and make the image as large as it allows.
- Exactly 4 frames, one per cell, in reading order (left to right along the top row, then left to right along the bottom row), in the numbered order below.
- POND GRUMP FACES RIGHT in every frame (toward the right side of the image), as if facing the family on the right of a battle screen. Seen from the side or three quarters, slightly from above.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on the creature. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on its edges. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.
- Same scale in every cell, exactly the scale and position of the figures in the underpainting, which already fills each cell as much as its widest pose allows. In every cell the feet or base rest on the same horizontal line as in the underpainting, with a small soft contact shadow directly under it. Nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.
- Draw ONLY POND GRUMP. No effects, motion lines, sparkles, other characters, props that are not part of it, text or word balloons.
- The same colors, details and level of painted detail in every frame.

THE 4 FRAMES
1. STANCE: battle stance, idle and ready, weight settled.
2. FLINCH: startled by a hit, recoiling a little, eyes shut or squinting.
3. ATTACK A: the wind-up for its signature attack, Soggy Slap.
4. ATTACK B: the attack landing.

Family friendly for ages 6 and up. Keep the flinch frame comic, never grim.

NEVER substitute. Do not add extra frames, merge two frames or repeat a pose. If anything is unclear, draw POND GRUMP in the pose described, facing right, with the shape and colors of the likeness in attachment 3.
